memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These are the regulations concerning defiling moulds in woollen or linen clothing, woven or knitted material, or any leather article, for pronouncing them clean or unclean." - Lev 13:59 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes quietly, the way a manual closes. These are the regulations. Fifty-nine verses of examining, waiting, and pronouncing, summarised in a single sentence.

Step back and look at the whole. What has God been doing in this long, strange chapter?

He has been teaching a people to take corruption seriously without treating one another carelessly. To examine honestly rather than hide. To wait rather than rush to judgement. To distinguish a scar from a wound, a rash from a disease, an ordinary human feature from a real problem. To act decisively when action is needed, and to welcome people back when the trouble has passed.

That is a remarkable education in wisdom, delivered through skin and cloth.

And all of it was pointing forward. The priest in this chapter could only diagnose. He had no cure. He could look, and wait, and pronounce — but he could not heal a single person. Every examination ended in a verdict, never a remedy.

Then came a Priest who could do what no priest before Him could. He does not merely inspect us and send us outside the camp. He touches the unclean and makes them clean. He carries the disease Himself. By His wounds we are healed (Isa 53:5; 1 Pet 2:24).

That is where this whole chapter has been heading.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God shown you most clearly through Leviticus 13?
2. Where do you need Christ to do what mere examination never could?
3. How will you live differently this week because of what you have read?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You are the Priest who does not only diagnose but heals. Where I am unclean, cleanse me; where I am excluded, bring me home. Amen.
